title: Scope of each track: small claims £10,000; fast track £25,000; intermediate track £100,000
principle: The small claims track is the normal track for claims of not more than £10,000; the fast track for claims of not more than £25,000 with a trial of no more than one day and limited expert evidence; the intermediate track for claims of not more than £100,000 brought by one or two claimants against one or two defendants that are unsuitable for the lower tracks; otherwise the multi-track. Credit hire claims are valued on the amount claimed, so most CCGUK files are small claims (fixed costs, lay representation possible).

citation: CPR 26.9 and 26.10 (road traffic personal injury limits); Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (RTA Small Claims Protocol)
title: Road traffic injury claims: £5,000 small claims limit for pain, suffering and loss of amenity (£1,000 for excepted claimants) and the Official Injury Claim portal
principle: For road traffic accidents on or after 31 May 2021 the small claims track is the normal track for a personal injury claim where damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenity are not more than £5,000 and the whole claim is not more than £10,000; where the CPR 26.10 exceptions apply (including vulnerable road users such as motorcyclists, cyclists and pedestrians, and child claimants) the injury limit stays at £1,000. title: QOCS exceptions: fundamental dishonesty; claims for the financial benefit of another
principle: Qualified one-way costs shifting (personal injury claims only) is lost, with the court's permission, where the claim is found on the balance of probabilities to be fundamentally dishonest, and may be enforced to the extent just where the proceedings include a claim made for the financial benefit of someone other than the claimant (the classic example being credit hire or subrogated vehicle damage pleaded in a PI claim). Credit hire claims without PI have no QOCS protection at all — the claimant is exposed to adverse costs on the fast/intermediate track, which is why weak-liability files should not run.

citation: PD 51ZE – Small Claims Track Automatic Referral to Mediation Pilot Scheme (as amended by the 193rd and 196th PD Updates)
title: Automatic referral to free mediation for defended small claims: extended to 6 April 2027 and, from 1 October 2026, including non-injury road traffic ("bent metal") claims
principle: PD 51ZE automatically refers defended small money claims (under £10,000) to a free one-hour HMCTS telephone mediation before the case progresses. The pilot began 22 May 2024 and originally ran to 21 May 2026 excluding road traffic accident and personal injury claims; the 193rd PD Update extended it to 6 April 2027 (aligned with the OCMC pilot PD 51R) and the 196th PD Update, in force 1 October 2026, brings non-personal-injury RTA claims into the mandatory scheme. From 1 October 2026 CCGUK should therefore expect every defended small claims credit hire/vehicle damage file to be referred to mediation; attend, prepared, with one clear number.

citation: PD 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot (RTA provisions; 187th, 190th and 193rd PD Updates)
title: OCMC mandation and the non-injury road traffic mediation pilot (from 28 July 2025)
principle: From 28 July 2025 eligible money claims must be issued online (OCMC or MCOL), and HMCTS began a 12-month pilot under PD 51R automatically referring defended OCMC claims worth under £10,000 that arise from a road traffic accident and include no personal injury element to free mediation; the 187th PD Update (in force 28 July 2025) removed the 'not a road traffic accident claim' exclusions from the headings above PD 51R paras 6.2 and 6.3 to make this possible. The OCMC pilot was extended to 1 October 2026 (190th Update) and then to April 2027 (193rd Update), and from 1 October 2026 PD 51ZE (196th Update) brings non-injury 'bent metal' RTA claims into the small claims mandatory mediation scheme as well. CCGUK should issue vehicle-damage and hire claims online on the client's behalf only as drafts for the client to submit (Legal Services Act 2007), and prepare every defended small claim for a one-hour telephone mediation with a single evidenced settlement figure.
